hypotheses.status: UNVALIDATED HYPOTHESIS; not built or scored
layers: Hydrologically conditioned drainage network and derived channel profiles
hypotheses.physical_signature: Look for a collinear, repeated same-sense lateral deflection or knickpoint across several neighboring channels/catchments, with a consistent cross-channel step. Score the network-level geometric motif, not an isolated high slope gradient.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: A young or low-throw blind fault can deform several channels before a clear scarp is mapped; a repeated displacement signature across catchments can persist where a single local slope-break detector is weak.
hypotheses.distinction_from_prior_repo_methods: BREAKLINE and SCARPPOL rank local slope-break or fall-line curvature pixels; this candidate is a drainage-graph / multi-catchment relationship. No drainage-network relay or aligned-knickpoint builder or holdout result was found in the reviewed tracked evidence.
named_non_fault_mimics: Lithologic or cementation boundaries that redirect multiple channels
Roads, canals, dams, or other drainage engineering
hypotheses.expected_value_and_cost: Potential information value: medium; implementation and validation cost: moderate to high. No numeric DTI expectation is assigned. A 100 m DEM may be too coarse for small offsets, so the first task would be a resolution / geomorphic falsification check.
required_data: Exact, hash-verified competition feature stack or an independently authorized DEM with matching footprint and CRS
Whole-fault-segment buffered holdout labels, used only through visible-fold catalogue features
Independent geomorphic controls for lithology, lake, and anthropogenic mimics

Grid-matched oriented cross-profiles and a reproducible scale / resolution sensitivity analysis
